key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves an aluminium MACE potential’s defect predictions while preserving tested near-equilibrium elastic and vibrational behavior.
engineering_relevance: The protocol supports more reliable atomistic simulations of defect dynamics and plasticity without sacrificing validated bulk-mechanical response.
method: Acquire configurations using conditional uncertainty over 144 readout weights, with within-batch covariance updates.
Iteratively update all model parameters while anchoring historical relative energies.
Gate updates against historical elastic-group energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: Four active-learning rounds using 32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates reduced mean development force error from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming sampling baselines; all three force-uncertainty runs met retention criteria.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested aluminium potential and bulk-response checks; broader transfer requires validation.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
